tiles.name: x10
tiles.subtitle: 14 MHz
tiles.result: x10 (20 dB) into a high impedance, x5 into 50 ohm, -3 dB near 14 MHz; clips at about +-4 V
notes: Non-inverting OPA810: gain 1 + 10 k / 1.1 k = 10.1, bandwidth 140 MHz / 10 = 14 MHz.  50 ohm at the input, 49.9 ohm
in series with the output (a 50 ohm load halves it: x5).  Keep the input under 0.4 V peak: the output clips at 4 V.

tiles.name: x100
tiles.subtitle: 1.4MHz
tiles.result: x100 (40 dB) into a high impedance, -3 dB near 1.4 MHz; keep the input under 40 mV peak
notes: Non-inverting OPA810: gain 1 + 10 k / 100 = 101, bandwidth 140 MHz / 100 = 1.4 MHz.  50 ohm at the input, 49.9 ohm
in series with the output.  For 40 dB out to 30 MHz use A4 (the OPA847 LNA); this tile is the FET-input, high-impedance
friendly x100 for everything slower.  (The plan's two stages of x10 did not fit the cell.)

tiles.name: LNA
tiles.subtitle: 30 MHz
tiles.result: x100 (40 dB) from 50 ohm, flat 1-30 MHz, about 3 dB noise figure from 50 ohm; keep the input under 30 mV peak
notes: Non-inverting OPA847 (3.9 GHz GBW at this gain, 0.85 nV/rtHz): 1 k / 10 ohm, so x101 and about 39 MHz.  Its
input noise with the 50 ohm termination's own noise gives a noise figure near 3 dB.  The op amp is stable only at
gains above 12 (it is decompensated): do not change Rg upward.  Pin 1 (no connection) carries the feedback node.

tiles.name: noise
tiles.subtitle: x100
tiles.result: the source resistor's Johnson noise x100: about 1.3 mV rms from 10 k, 0.4 mV from 1 k, 0.16 mV (the amplifier itself) shorted
notes: 4kTR: 12.9 nV/rtHz from 10 k at room temperature, x100 and the LT6230's 2 MHz: 1.3 mV rms.  Both DIP ways off
with nothing in the socket leaves +IN open: switch one on, or plug a resistor (100 ohm to 10 k) into the socket.
Keep the scope AC-coupled: 600 nA of bias current puts 0.6 V of DC on the output with 10 k.

tiles.name: 1-bit ADC
tiles.result: a one-bit stream on Pmod IO7 whose density follows IN; the FPGA closes the loop through Pmod IO8 (the handbook's gateware)
notes: First-order delta-sigma: the comparator decides, the FPGA registers the bit and feeds it back through 10 k into the
10 k / 10 nF integrator (1.6 kHz; clock the loop at 1-10 MHz).  IN takes 0 to 3.3 V, or +-1.5 V about the 1.65 V reference
if you AC-couple.  Both Pmod lines are 3.3 V logic; the tile runs on the 3.3 V rail.

tiles.name: PLL 4046
tiles.result: VCO OUT locks to a 50-200 kHz square or sine on IN; pin 9 is the demodulated FM, pin 13 the phase detector
notes: CD74HC4046A: R1 10 k, C1 1 nF put the VCO near 100 kHz (R2 open: it can go down to 0).  PC2 (the edge-triggered
tri-state detector) through 10 k / 100 n into VCOin: a lag filter, so expect ringing on lock.  IN self-biases
through 100 n / 1 k (any level above 0.4 V peak).  VCO OUT is 5 V CMOS through 470 ohm.  Probe pins 9 and 13.

tiles.name: heat
tiles.result: 0.83 W into the board when Pmod IO6 is high (the FET's drain), 10 mV/K + 500 mV on OUT
notes: Two 15 ohm in series: 30 ohm, 170 mA, 0.83 W from the switched 5 V when Pmod IO6 is high (10 k keeps it off otherwise).
The TMP235 reads 750 mV at 25 C and climbs 10 mV per kelvin.  A feedback-control experiment: hold the TMP235 at a
set point with the FPGA's PWM.  (The plan's NTC divider did not fit the cell beside the two 2512s.)

tiles.name: mixer
tiles.subtitle: MC1496
tiles.result: IF OUT = RF x LO (sum and difference frequencies, about 0.3 V peak per volt of RF at 0.3 V of LO); a balanced mixer, the carrier mostly cancels
notes: Gilbert cell on +-5 V: signal pair at ground (51 ohm), carrier pair at 2.5 V (51 ohm to the 10 k / 10 k bias), 1 mA
per side (3.9 k), 1.5 k loads.  Keep RF under 0.3 V and LO near 0.3 V peak (above that the carrier pair just switches,
which is fine for a product detector).  IF OUT is single-ended from pin 6 through 100 n: a 1.5 k source, so read it
with a high-impedance input, not 50 ohm.  No carrier-null trimmer: expect -40 dB of LO feedthrough.

tiles.name: light
tiles.subtitle: LED + PD
tiles.result: 45 mA of LED current per volt on DRIVE IN (0-1 V, blanked while Pmod IO5 is high); PD OUT climbs 10 V per mA of photocurrent
notes: The current source: the op amp holds 22 ohm at the input voltage, so the LED carries V / 22 ohm (0.9 V is the LED's
full 40 mA; above 1.1 V the op amp runs out of headroom).  A 2N7002 from Pmod IO5 shorts the input: TTL modulation to
a few MHz.  The photodiode (5 V reverse) into 10 k with 10 pF: 1.6 MHz; daylight on the PD gives millivolts, the LED
of a second board across a desk gives tens.  The LED looks out of the board's right edge, the photodiode looks up.

tiles.name: ultrasound
tiles.result: a 40 kHz burst from Pmod IO4/IO3 leaves the TX transducer; its echo arrives x100 on RX OUT (hold a reflector over the board)
notes: Drive IN1/IN2 (Pmod IO4, IO3) in antiphase at 40 kHz for 8-20 cycles: the bridge puts 10 V peak to peak across the TX
transducer.  The RX transducer's 10 nF / 3.9 k high-pass (4 kHz) feeds an OPA810 at x100 (1.4 MHz: the transducer's
own resonance sets the band).  Time of flight at 343 m/s: 5.8 us per mm there and back.  Put the two transducers
in pins 1 and 5 (10.16 mm; their leads are 10 mm apart).

tiles.name: audio
tiles.result: a speaker on SPK follows AUDIO IN (2.5 W into 4 ohm) or the one-bit stream on Pmod IO2 (10 k / 10 n); MIC OUT is the electret x100
notes: PAM8302A: 1 u couples AUDIO IN to IN+ (IN- grounded through 1 u), the one-bit DAC on Pmod IO2 arrives through 10 k
into 10 n (1.6 kHz) at the same node, so both play.  BYP 1 u, SD high: on with the tile.  The electret (pin 1 is the
+ side, 2.2 k from VS) through 1 u into an OPA810 at x100: a few hundred millivolts for speech.

tiles.name: power
tiles.subtitle: USB-C 5 V in: +5, -5, +3.3 out
tiles.result: +5 V from the USB-C (up to 1.5 A), -5 V at 40 mA, +3.3 V at 300 mA; the green LED says 5 V is in, the red one that -5 V is up
notes: USB-C power only: 5.1 k on each CC asks any source for 5 V.  A 2 A PTC, a 5 V TVS (clamps at 9.2 V) and 20 uF.
The LM2664 charge pump makes -5 V for the op-amp tiles (40 mA: four tiles at 10 mA); it is not switched per tile, an op
amp with its +5 V removed draws nothing.  The TPS7A2033 makes 3.3 V for the comparator and the lines that meet the FPGA.
The socket along the top carries +5, ground, -5, ground, +3.3: the bench's rails for a breadboard experiment.

back_text: AMOD-A: active blocks on USB-C power.  Each tile
has a slide switch (up: on) and SMA jacks: cable
DAC OUT to IN, OUT to ADC IN.  The Pmod plug (left)
takes the FPGA's lines; the handbook has the rest.
